hobbies.name: Balisong flipping
paragraphs: I enjoy balisong flipping. A balisong, also called a butterfly knife, has two handles that rotate around the blade. Flipping involves learning tricks and connecting those movements into sequences.

hobbies.name: Speedcubing
paragraphs: Speedcubing is solving a Rubik’s Cube as quickly as you can. My fastest solve was 13 seconds, though that was a while ago.
I’ve recently gotten back into it and am practicing to get close to that time again.

hobbies.name: Basketball
paragraphs: I also like playing basketball. It’s another way I enjoy spending time away from my desk.

experience.label: Hardware & technical support

experience.organization: UC Santa Barbara · Summer Research Academies
experience.label: Computational social science
experience.summary: Studying relationships between media outlet reputation, political bias among Reddit audiences, and interactions across communities.
points: Co-authored a research paper analyzing the connection between media outlet reputation and political bias among Reddit audiences and their interactions, presenting it at the Capstone Seminar.

Applied VADER sentiment analysis, correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression to study relationships between media reputation, article tone, political topics, audience responses, and audience interactions with other communities.

projects.name: Sourcecado
projects.headline: Keeping contacts, conversations, and tasks connected.
projects.description: Sourcecado is a local-first AI application for managing sponsor contacts. I developed shared CRM features across chats, integrated Gmail synchronization, and built recovery safeguards so interrupted workflows can resume with clear boundaries around external actions.

points.title: Shared task management across chats
points.text: Built shared tasks with descriptions, due dates, AI suggestions, and urgency labels, keeping contact-related work accessible across conversations rather than isolated in a single chat.

points.title: Gmail synchronization that preserves progress
points.text: Implemented persistent checkpoints, message deduplication, and contact matching. Synchronization can recover its progress after failures while preserving conversation history and avoiding duplicate messages.

points.title: Recovery that accounts for uncertain outcomes
points.text: Used saved checkpoints and execution records to distinguish work that is safe to resume from external actions whose outcomes are unknown. Those uncertain actions require review before retrying.

architecture.label: React interface connects to FastAPI for CRM workflows, with SQLite for persistent storage.

projects.preview: Shared tasks across chats, checkpointed Gmail sync, and recovery safeguards for interrupted AI workflows.

projects.name: Doodle2Design
projects.headline: Turning a rough sketch into a website redesign.
projects.description: A full-stack application that translates sketches, uploaded images, and visual preferences into redesigned web pages. I built the application and integrated OpenAI models for image analysis and page generation. The project placed second in a hackathon hosted by Amazon and Google employees.

architecture.label: User sketches, images, and visual preferences guide OpenAI analysis and generation of redesigned web pages.

points.title: A complete path from visual input to generated pages
points.text: Built the full-stack workflow around user sketches, uploaded images, and visual preferences, connecting those inputs to image analysis and website generation through the OpenAI API.

points.title: Generation guided by 30 design templates
points.text: Compared user inputs with a collection of 30 design templates to guide the generated layout, style, and visual consistency, giving the redesign process a concrete set of references.

points.title: A mood dataset based on agreement across models
points.text: Created a dataset of 50 images with mood labels generated by models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. Retained the labels identified by all three models rather than relying on a single model's interpretation.

projects.preview: Sketches and visual preferences become website redesigns, guided by 30 design templates. Second-place hackathon project.

projects.name: Campus Event Finder
projects.headline: Making campus events easier to find and manage.
projects.description: A full-stack web application for students to discover events by date, category, and campus location. I built the event search experience and a Flask REST API backed by SQLite, with authentication and input validation around account access and event submissions.

points.title: Search around a student's plans
points.text: Built search and filtering by date, category, and campus location so students can narrow the event list to activities that fit their schedule and interests.

points.title: A REST API with persistent event storage
points.text: Designed Flask endpoints for creating, retrieving, filtering, and deleting events. Used SQLite to store event data persistently and support the application's event-management workflow.

points.title: Account protection and validated submissions
points.text: Integrated user authentication to protect accounts and input validation to prevent invalid event submissions, handling both access and data quality at the application boundary.

architecture.label: A student filters events in a web interface, backed by a Flask REST API and SQLite storage.
